steps.title: Install PHP dependencies (Composer)
steps.why: api/composer.json declares the PHP dependencies and composer.lock pins them; composer install installs exactly the locked versions.
notes: Composer also runs the project's "post-autoload-dump" script: Illuminate\Foundation\ComposerScripts::postAutoloadDump && @php artisan package:discover --ansi

steps.title: Install JavaScript dependencies (npm)
steps.why: api/package.json declares the dependencies; package-lock.json exists. The command installs exactly the locked versions and does not modify the lockfile.
notes: If this fails because the lockfile is out of date, run "npm install" instead (it may change the lockfile).

steps.title: Create .env from .env.example
steps.why: The app reads its configuration from .env, which is not committed; api/.env.example is the template. CI (ci.yml) runs "cp .env.example .env" (recipe agrees).

steps.title: Generate the application key (APP_KEY)
steps.why: Laravel encrypts sessions and cookies with APP_KEY, and the template leaves it empty. Without it every page fails with "No application encryption key has been specified".

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: generate the application key (app_key)

steps.title: Link public/storage to storage/app/public
steps.why: Uploaded files on the public disk are served through this link. The app starts without it, but uploads and generated files 404.
notes: On Windows, creating a symbolic link needs Developer Mode or an administrator prompt; this tool never elevates.

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: link public/storage to storage/app/public

steps.title: Start mysql, redis with Docker Compose
steps.why: docker-compose.yml defines mysql 8.0 and redis 7, which the app needs. Compose reads the env file in its folder for passwords and ports.
notes: Creates containers and volumes outside the project folder, and downloads images on first run.
If you already run mysql/redis on this machine, skip this step and point the env file at it.
Stop them later with: docker compose stop

steps.title: Create the database tables (migrations)
steps.why: database/migrations holds the schema. The app's first request fails on missing tables until they are created.
notes: Needs the database server running and DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_DATABASE, DB_USERNAME and DB_PASSWORD in the env file to match it; the database itself must exist.

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: create the database tables (migrations)

steps.title: Fill the database with seed data
steps.why: database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php exists. Seeding adds sample or required records (often an admin user); read the seeder before running it.

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: fill the database with seed data

steps.title: Build the frontend assets
steps.why: Blade templates load compiled CSS and JavaScript (@vite reads public/build/manifest.json; mix() reads public/mix-manifest.json). Without a build, pages fail or render unstyled unless a dev/watch server runs.

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: build the frontend assets

steps.title: Install JavaScript dependencies (pnpm)
steps.why: web/package.json declares the dependencies; package.json sets packageManager: "pnpm@9.15.0" (lockfile, ci agree). The command installs exactly the locked versions and does not modify the lockfile.
notes: If this fails because the lockfile is out of date, run "pnpm install" instead (it may change the lockfile).

steps.title: Create .env.local from .env.example
steps.why: The app reads its configuration from .env.local, which is not committed; web/.env.example is the template. Next.js reads .env.local.

steps.title: Build web for production
steps.why: Only needed for the production run target; the dev server builds on the fly.

run.name: dev
run.title: Start the Laravel app with its dev script (server, queue, logs, Vite)

evidence.detail: composer run dev listens on port 8000 by default

run.why: composer.json defines a dev script, the maintainers' own way to start everything together. It runs `php artisan pail`, which needs the pcntl extension that PHP for Windows lacks. On Windows run `php artisan serve` and the Vite dev server separately.

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: start the laravel app with its dev script (server, queue, logs, vite)

run.name: serve
run.title: Start the Laravel development server

evidence.detail: php artisan serve listens on port 8000 by default

run.why: php artisan serve listens on http://127.0.0.1:8000 by default.

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: start the laravel development server

run.name: queue
run.title: Process queued jobs
run.why: QUEUE_CONNECTION is not sync, so jobs wait in a queue until a worker processes them.

run.name: test
run.title: Run the test suite
run.why: phpunit.xml configures the tests; php artisan test runs them.

evidence.detail: Laravel recipe: run the test suite

run.name: start
run.title: Serve web (next server)
run.why: web/package.json defines "start": next start (needs a build first).

conflicts.message: api/.env.example sets DB_HOST=mysql, the name of a Compose service. That name only resolves between containers; with the app running on your machine use DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 (the published port).
conflicts.rule: compose service names resolve only inside Docker
